statement: When a runbook lists one set in two places, the copies drift. A runbook defined the files whose PRs need re-judging twice: in a freeze check (section 7) and in a close-and-reopen loop (section 8). The two lists diverged. The loop drew its files from a narrower configuration than the freeze check, so it missed logs whose content is also gated on a signature, and the PRs touching them would not have been re-judged. Neither list was wrong on its own terms; the defect was that nothing tied them together. Rules: when one set is listed in two places, derive both from one definition, or check mechanically that both name the same files.
